scenes.tts: One human cell holds billions of protein molecules, from about ten thousand kinds. You want one. Which molecule is doing this job, and can you hold it in a tube, free of everything else? In the nineteen twenties, leading chemists held that enzymes were not proteins.
scenes.visual: A cell pours a crowd of many grey dots into a tube; one hidden dot wears a question mark, and an empty second tube asks whether it can be held alone.

scenes.tts: Start with an assay, a way to detect the target in a tube where you cannot see it. Lactate dehydrogenase consumes N A D H, which absorbs light at three hundred forty nanometres. N A D plus does not, so absorbance falls. Then break the cells and spin. A gentle spin pellets nuclei, a harder one mitochondria, a harder one the smallest vesicles.
scenes.visual: A cuvette with a light beam and a falling absorbance trace, then a homogenate spun at three speeds, pellets forming.

scenes.tts: After each step, run the assay again. Specific activity is units of activity divided by milligrams of total protein. It rises when a step removes contaminant without destroying the target. Salting out uses solubility: ammonium sulfate drops proteins out at different salt concentrations, leaving many contaminants behind. Gel filtration uses size. Large proteins cannot enter the pores, so take the short path and elute first. Small ones come last.
scenes.visual: A scoreboard of specific and total activity at the side while a salt cut drops some proteins and leaves others, and a gel filtration column releases the large dots first.

scenes.tts: Ion exchange uses charge, and opposite charges stick. Below its p I, a protein is net positive and binds a cation exchanger. Above it, the protein is net negative and binds an anion exchanger. Raise the salt, and it lets go. Affinity uses beads that carry something only the target recognizes. The target binds, the rest flows through, and free ligand displaces it. If you know a binding partner, start with affinity.
scenes.visual: Charged beads hold oppositely charged dots, salt releases them; bait beads catch only the target and free ligand floods it off; a short rule closes it.

scenes.tts: Read the purification table. Total protein and activity both fall, because protein is lost, and some enzyme with it. Specific activity should rise at every step. In this idealised example, it climbs from about ten to thirty thousand units per milligram, a three thousandfold purification, while yield slides to roughly a third. In Benovic's real run, four columns gave about twenty thousandfold, with twelve percent recovered.
scenes.visual: An idealised purification table fills in, specific activity rising and yield falling, then the real Benovic run replaces it: four column chips, fold bar up, recovery bar down.

scenes.tts: Purity can strip away a partner. Benovic's kinase batch, purified only three hundred fifty-fold, cut a receptor's G-protein activation by up to eighty percent. The twenty thousandfold pure enzyme cut it far less, because a second protein, arrestin, had apparently been removed. So test the pure fraction on the effect.
scenes.visual: Receptor kinase with its arrestin partner cuts G-protein activation a lot; the purer kinase without arrestin cuts it only slightly; then the control.
scenes.caption: Purity can strip away a partner. Benovic's kinase batch, purified only 350-fold, cut a receptor's G-protein activation by up to 80 percent. scenes.tts: In nineteen twenty-six, Sumner crystallized urease from jack bean extract. Dissolved, the crystals gave tests for protein and very high urease activity. Enzymes can be proteins. In January nineteen twenty-two, James Collip raised alcohol in steps to trap insulin in a semipure form, and his extract worked in patient Leonard Thompson. Purification made insulin a drug.
scenes.visual: Two panels: jack bean extract to crystals that test positive for protein and urease (Sumner, 1926); rising alcohol steps to a vial that works in a patient (Collip, 1922).

scenes.tts: Stanley Cohen's group ran an E G F affinity column. Receptor, kinase and substrate came out together, and the kinase phosphorylated tyrosine. Labelling later showed the receptor is the kinase. In nineteen ninety-seven, Alessi, Cohen and colleagues purified a kinase five hundred thousandfold. It activates Akt only with certain lipids, which a purified system can test directly. A pure fraction speaks only for the assay you followed. Test it on the biological effect.
scenes.visual: An EGF-bait column pulls out one band; tyrosine gets a phosphate; a purified kinase switches on Akt only when a lipid is added; the rule in a box.
